summary: The article describes a wave of national cybersecurity R&D investment from September 2023 to April 2024. It covers a pledge to double R&D funding, quantum, AI threat detection, critical infrastructure protection, information sharing, workforce grants, and an ethics board. It argues that sustained investment and collaboration could make cybersecurity proactive by 2030.
one_line: National cybersecurity strategies from late 2023 to April 2024 boost R&D funding across quantum, AI, infrastructure, workforce, collaboration and ethics.
key_facts: On September 15, 2023, Dr. Elaine Marcus unveiled a strategy at the International Cybersecurity Symposium to double cybersecurity R&D investment over the next five years.
The R&D pledge targets quantum computing, artificial intelligence (AI) in threat detection, and fortification of critical infrastructure.
The Quantum Initiative Act was passed on October 4, 2023, as an R&D program to harness quantum technologies for cybersecurity.
Dr. Samuel Li, Director of the National Quantum Coordination Office, leads the quantum initiative, which promises a robust framework by 2025.
Rachel Torres, an AI specialist, unveiled a project on November 12, 2023, that uses AI algorithms to predict and neutralize cyber threats before they materialize.
The National Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Center is interested in integrating such AI systems into its monitoring by 2028.
On December 3, 2023, the National Infrastructure Protection Plan was updated to include an R&D fund focused on cybersecurity for critical infrastructure such as power grids and financial networks.
Engineers like Kendra Johnson are developing redundant systems, secure communication protocols, and vulnerability assessments for infrastructure.
The Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act (CISA) was revised on January 9, 2024, to streamline threat intelligence sharing, leading to cross-border think tanks and R&D hubs.
The National Science Foundation announced significant grants on February 14, 2024, for universities pioneering cybersecurity education.
Dr. Jennifer Holt chairs the Cybersecurity Talent Initiative and stresses a workforce that builds secure systems and uses them responsibly.
The Cyber Ethics Review Board was convened on March 20, 2024, to set guidelines for responsible use of cybersecurity technologies.
The Cybersecurity 2030 Summit, convened on April 25, 2024, predicted that with sustained R&D investment cybersecurity could become a proactive force by 2030.
